studies.summary: Thirty independent simulated focus groups mapped friction across consumer and business life, each with participants representing conflicting sides. Independently strong pains: mechanic distrust and the 83% second-opinion ritual; micro field-service revenue leaking through lost paper and whiteboards; hourly workers photo-proofing schedules and paystubs against silent changes and short-pay; creator proofing selections never returning to the catalog; deposit disputes without a neutral condition record; 63M US family caregivers policing medical logistics; and travel-disruption claims reconstructed from nothing. A parallel 30-question service-disruption hunt and a cross-domain-transfer and tech-capability scan converged on the same clusters. The round then novelty-tested 40 concepts and found the mobile-pain market saturated with 2025-2026 clones; the two surviving VALIDATE-FIRST candidates are a photo-to-invoice un-invoiced-work detector for micro trades and a return-intake evidence pack for resellers.
